text: Field Marshal's Threads is the Alliance PvP-Epic set for warlocks. It consists of six pieces. Field Marshal Oslight is a human quest giver located in Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands.

.]] The Field of Strife is an area located in the center of Alterac Valley. It is the "no man's land" of Alterac Valley. It was previously occupied by NPC forces from both Stormpike Guards and Frostwolf Clan. Those NPC forces have since been removed. Since their removal, very little fighting actually takes place in the Field of Strife because it lacks strategic value. However, this area is still used to summon Ivus the Forest Lord and Lokholar the Ice Lord. Fighting would often occur here before and during the summoning.
Feruul is a draenei located at the Trader's Tier in the Exodar. During the Battle for the Exodar, he was inside Velen's protective shield.

Fertile Spores drop from various mobs in Zangarmarsh, namely the sporebats and spore walkers. Once a player is with Sporeggar, these can be handed into Gshaff in the Sporeggar town as a repeatable quest, giving reputation. 6 fertile spores can be handed in each time.
Field Marshal Brock is a human quest giver located at Honor Point - a small camp just east of Forge Camp: Mageddon in the Hellfire Peninsula.
Fhwoor Smash! is an escort quest only obtainable after reaching with Sporeggar. Also important, Fhwoor does not complete the quest, a nearby sporeling does.
Fiend Slayer Boots can be obtained by winning the Chess Event in Karazhan.

Feulia, a half-Kaldorei archer, was a member of a group of treasure hunters who were led by Drann. This group also included Dumont, Makil, Stonehoof, Renmar, and Talario. She helped battle against centaur and other monsters which were guarding an ancient altar and sealed shrine in the Barrens. She killed several of the guardians. While she pulled one of her enchanted arrows from the eye socket of a fallen wildkin, her companions prepared for the ritual on the Altar. Feulia then climbed a nearby ridge for a better view, watchful for another attack. After her companions released an elemental prince, she was likely taken to the Firelands with them.

Fiend is the first story in Warcraft: Legends Volume 3 and the third part of the Trag saga. *Written by Richard A. Knaak *Art by Jae-Hwan Kim *Edited by Tim Beedle

The Festering Pools is an area once part of Geyser Fields that has been overrun with the Scourge from the downed necropolis, Talramas, in the Borean Tundra. Water in this area is strangely absent. While the Geyser Fields stinks of sulfur, it is far here where the undead are. Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the area is still under the control of the undead.

Festergut is a boss in the Plagueworks wing of the Icecrown Citadel raid. It's mainly a DPS race gear check, with only limited tactics involved. He has sometimes been called "Patchwerk 3.3". This boss is available since January 5, 2010 on US servers and January 6 on EU servers.

Festergut's Acidic Blood can be found on the corpse of in the Plagueworks of Icecrown Citadel in 25-player mode, and is a quest objective for The Sacred and the Corrupt. The blood is not group loot! Only one drops per kill in 25-player mode.

Field Medic Penny is a dwarven priestess part of the Hodir encounter in Ulduar. She, along with her party is trapped in blocks of ice and must be freed to help against the frost titans attacks. If the raid is in the 25man version of Ulduar then she will be replaced by Field Medic Jessi.

Field Medic Jessi is a dwarven priestess part of the Hodir encounter in Ulduar. She, along with her party is trapped in blocks of ice and must be freed to help against the frost titans attacks. If the raid is in the 10man version of Ulduar then she will be replaced by Field Medic Penny.
Fezzik's Autocannon is obtained from the Argent Crusade Tribute Chest with 25-44 attempts remaining.
Fibrous Vine was an objective of Once More, With Eeling (beta) before the quest was changed.

Field Journal is provided for Orcs Can Write? and is found on the corpse of the in the Kaja'mite Cavern. It is also the objective of The Enemy of My Enemy. The contents of the journal seems to indicate that the captain of the Draka's Fury intentionally led the ship to an Alliance ambush.
Fickle Heart is a quest item for She Loves Me, She Loves Me NOT!.

__NOTOC__ Field Agent Kaartish is a draenei agent of the Argent Crusade seeking to cleanse the Plaguelands. Kaartish intended to find out what prevented local wildlife to heal. He discovered a new blight that was infecting the wildlife and that remains of the Cult of the Damned led by Instructor Malicia were inoculating the animals. Thus, the draenei sent adventurers to kill her and disrupt their reanimating operations.
Fiasco Sizzlegrin is a goblin located in Tenebrous Cavern in Abyssal Depths and in Shimmering Expanse.
Field Dressing is a Tier 1 talent in the Warrior's Arms tree.

Feronas seems to be a huge admirer of Illidan Stormrage, as most of his quests revolves around reliving Illidan's recently earned freedom, from his first fight with Arthas in Felwood up to the day he killed Tichondrius after consuming the Skull of Gul'dan.
Fiendish Whip is a common archaeology artifact that requires 45 Orc Archaeology Fragments to complete. Two keystones may be used to complete this artifact.

The bulk of the Fields of Blood are taken up by the competing camps at Vendetta Point (Horde) and Forward Command (Alliance). Fibi is, along with Binzella, Pank and Vink one of four bankers in the Orgrimmar Counting House which is located in the Valley of Honor of Orgrimmar. After Vol'jin's death, she was seen speaking with Vink outside of the building.
Fielding Chesterhill is a cooking trainer found in the town of Duskhaven in Gilneas. He is located in the inn on the ground floor.

After the big Dook is defeated all of the hozen become afraid of the heroes and avoid them.

's Fields of the Eternal Hunt.]] The Fields of Eternal Hunt are a section of the mythical Halls of Valor, the home of the Valarjar. Unlike much of the rest of the Halls, this is a large, outdoor area filled with lush vegetation and abundant game. Here, Odyn's chosen train and compete in hunting great beasts. The area itself is reminiscent of the landscape of Stormheim, and can only be accessed through the Ephemeral Way. The Envoy of the Hunt is charged with seeking out worthy animals for the hunting grounds. __NOTOC__ The Fetid Crypt is a large chamber below Atul'Aman in Vol'dun, accessed from the Abandoned Passage. After General Jakra'zet stole the keystones to Atul'Aman, Bladeguard Kaja and Warguard Rakera chased after him into the crypt but were ensnared by tentacles. Vorrik and a Horde adventurer caught up with and freed them, after which the group continued to the Blood Font to confront Jakra'zet.

The Fetish of the Dark Caverns can be looted from the Challenger's Cache at the end of a successful level 4 or higher Mythic+ dungeon. Only classes with a tank specialization can loot it. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 1 of the Anima of Life and Death Essence and leave behind a Frayed Fetish.

The Fetish of the Deep Dungeons can be looted from the Challenger's Cache at the end of a successful level 7 or higher Mythic+ dungeon. Only classes with a tank specialization can loot it. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 2 of the Anima of Life and Death Essence and leave behind a Frayed Fetish.

The Fetish of the Hidden Labyrinths is created by combining 8 Focused Life Anima, which can be looted from your weekly Grand Challenger's Bounty in Boralus or Zuldazar. Only classes with a tank specialization can create it. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 3 of the Anima of Life and Death Essence and leave behind a Frayed Fetish.

The Fetish of the Gilded Catacombs could be purchased for 75 Titan Residuum from Thaumaturge Vashreen in Boralus or Dazar'alor after completing Battle for Azeroth Keystone Master: Season Three. Infusing the item at the Heart Forge will grant Rank 4 of the Anima of Life and Death Essence and leave behind a Frayed Fetish.
